title: sufr panics when its output is piped into a reader that stops early, such as head
body:
`sufr` panics when the reader of its stdout closes early:

```text
$ sufr summarize data/expected/uniprot-masked.sufr | head
...
thread 'main' panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1166:9:
failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)
```

At `f866248`, `summarize`, `list`, `locate` and `extract` all panic this way when piped into `head -1`. `count` with seven queries printed too little to show it. Rust ignores `SIGPIPE`, so a write to a closed pipe returns an `EPIPE` error, and `println!` turns that error into a panic. The output that reached `head` is correct; the panic message on stderr and the exit status are what go wrong.

## Open

- Whether `main` should treat a broken pipe as a normal exit, or the commands should write through a handle whose errors they return.
